fields.overview: Allura Red AC is a synthetic red dye, also called FD&C Red 40. The principal colouring substance is an azo compound supplied as a salt, with small amounts of other colouring substances and uncoloured salts allowed by the specification. Commercial material is a dark red powder or granules. It adds or restores red colour in foods.
fields.origin: Manufacturers first prepare an aromatic diazo intermediate and then join it to a sulphonated naphthol compound. The resulting dye is purified as a salt. This is chemical synthesis; the red pigment is not extracted from a fruit or insect. The EU specification describes the sodium form and also permits calcium and potassium forms.
fields.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; flavoured drinks; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products; unripened cheese excluding products falling in category 16.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.

fields.overview: Gelatine is a mixture of animal-derived proteins obtained by partially breaking down collagen. It absorbs water and softens in cold water, then dissolves when heated. On cooling, the solution forms a gel, which explains its gelling function in food. JECFA also identifies stabilising, emulsifying and crystallisation-control functions. The commercial ingredient can be supplied as sheets, flakes or powder, with grades that differ in gel strength.
fields.origin: Gelatine is manufactured by partially hydrolysing collagen from animal tissues such as skin, tendons, ligaments and bones. The protein is extracted and processed into dried sheets, flakes or powder. It is an animal-derived ingredient; the specification does not identify a single animal species for every product.
fields.dietary_restrictions: Ordinary gelatine is made from animal collagen and is therefore unsuitable for vegan and vegetarian diets. Halal and kosher suitability depend on the animal species, slaughter and processing arrangements, and product certification; the E code alone does not establish those conditions.

No current country-wide food-use ban was confirmed in the regulatory sources checked in 2026.

gaps: Gelatine: animal species and halal/kosher certification were not established for a particular commercial product; no universal religious suitability is asserted.

fields.overview: Mannitol is a sugar alcohol whose specified additive preparations can contain small amounts of other polyols. It provides sweetness when added to the food or used in a table-top sweetener preparation. Specified mannitol can be made by hydrogenating glucose- or fructose-containing solutions, or by fermentation with a suitable Zygosaccharomyces rouxii yeast strain. The specified material is supplied as white powder or crystalline material. The specification identifies water solubility as one of its properties.
fields.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain cocoa and Chocolate products as covered by Directive 2000/36/EC; other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; fruit juices as defined by Directive 2001/112/EC and vegetable juices; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.

fields.overview: Konjac preparations contain glucomannan, a polysaccharide composed of glucose and mannose from the tuber of Amorphophallus konjac. Its emulsifying role is to help form or maintain mixtures of oil and water in the finished food. Konjac gum and konjac glucomannan are obtained from konjac tubers. Water extraction produces the gum, while washing konjac flour with aqueous ethanol yields the glucomannan preparation. One specified form is supplied as white powder.

fields.overview: Cassia gum is the purified ground seed endosperm of Cassia tora and Cassia obtusifolia, consisting mainly of a galactomannan polysaccharide. fields.overview: Polysorbate 20 is a mixture of ethoxylated sorbitol-derived esters of lauric acid; its preparation contains approximately 20 oxyethylene units per sorbitol-derived unit. White beeswax is made by bleaching yellow beeswax. The specified material is supplied as white crystalline material or small sheets. The specification describes it as effectively insoluble in water.
fields.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain cocoa and Chocolate products as covered by Directive 2000/36/EC; other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; coffee, coffee extracts; sweet baked goods.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
fields.banned_in:
Approved in the EU.
No current country-wide food-use ban was confirmed in the regulatory sources checked in 2026.
The permissions checked in 2026 apply only to the specified preparations, food uses and conditions.

Permitted food categories and concentration limits depend on the jurisdiction and the particular food.
fields.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; fruit juices as defined by Directive 2001/112/EC and vegetable juices; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products; sauces; extra jam and extra jelly as defined by Directive 2001/113/EC.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.

fields.overview: Oxystearin is a mixture of glycerides containing partially oxidised stearic and other fatty acids. The US applications are in vegetable oils and shortenings, with a maximum of 0.125% of the oil or shortening weight.

fields.overview: Bakers yeast glycan is processed cell-wall material from Saccharomyces cerevisiae yeast. Its food functions include thickening, stabilising, emulsifying and adjusting texture. FDA describes use in salad dressings, dessert and sour-cream alternatives, cheese-spread alternatives and some snack dips.

fields.overview: Peptones are mixtures of amino acids and short protein chains obtained by partial breakdown of proteins. The starting proteins may come from animal tissues, milk, eggs or soy. FDA describes production using suitable enzymes, acids or heat. The ingredient has nutrient, processing-aid and surface-active functions, and its composition depends on the starting protein and treatment.
fields.origin: Produced by partial hydrolysis of proteins using suitable proteolytic enzymes, acids or heat. FDA's permitted starting materials include milk proteins, egg albumin, animal tissue, gelatine and soy protein isolate. Peptones can therefore be plant- or animal-derived, depending on the actual starting protein.

fields.overview: Succinylated monoglycerides are mixtures of succinic-acid esters of mono- and diglycerides. These applications have different concentration limits, and the starting fat source is not fixed by the name.

fields.uses: Used as an emulsifier in liquid or plastic shortenings and as a dough conditioner in bread baking. The US maxima are 3% of shortening weight and 0.5% of flour weight, respectively, subject to the relevant food standards.

fields.overview: Mineral oil is a liquid mixture of petroleum hydrocarbons, distinct from semi-solid petrolatum and solid petroleum wax. FDA specifies white mineral oil for limited food-processing uses, with purity requirements for the commercial material. Its applications include release, lubrication, dust control and protective coating in specified processes. The permitted purpose and amount depend on the food or operation. A food-use specification for refined oil cannot be applied to an unrefined petroleum product.

fields.overview: Guaiac resin is the resin preparation also recorded as gum guaiac or guaiacum. JECFA identifies it as an antioxidant under INS 314. Its historical technological role is to slow oxidative deterioration in food. The retained evaluation is from 1973, so it describes an older preparation and assessment rather than demonstrating a current food-market application.

fields.overview: Ethyl hydroxyethyl cellulose is a chemically modified cellulose ether containing both ethyl and hydroxyethyl groups. JECFA also names it as the 2-hydroxyethyl ether of ethyl cellulose. Its recorded food functions include emulsifying, thickening and stabilising. It is a polymer preparation rather than a small, single-formula molecule. This historical entry has its own identity within the modified-cellulose group.

fields.overview: Edible bone phosphate is a mixture of calcium phosphates containing mainly tribasic calcium phosphate. JECFA describes the material as a heterogeneous residual preparation, so it should not be equated with every purified calcium-phosphate salt. Its listed functions include emulsifying, retaining moisture and binding metal ions. The historical entry describes the bone-phosphate preparation specifically, while related phosphates have separate identities.

fields.overview: Vermiculite is a natural hydrated silicate containing magnesium, aluminium and iron. It is supplied in mineral preparations that can include heat-expanded material. The EFSA record concerns its proposed use as a binder and anti-caking material in animal feed. That application concerns feed consistency and handling. It does not establish a typical human-food use for this historical dataset entry.

The specified mineral preparation is distinct from the broader sepiolitic-clay mixture.

fields.overview: Lignosulphonates are lignin-derived polymer preparations obtained during sulphite pulping of plant material. These feed uses do not establish permission for direct addition of every lignosulphonate to human food.

fields.overview: Natrolite-phonolite is a natural mixture of aluminosilicate minerals from volcanic rock. The preparation assessed by EFSA contains natrolite together with feldspar and other mineral components. It is made by quarrying, crushing, heat conditioning and fine grinding. Its proposed technological use is to reduce caking in animal feed. The mineral mixture and source deposit are part of the identity of the preparation assessed.
fields.origin: Mineral-derived. The assessed preparation is made from volcanic rock quarried in the Kaiserstuhl area of Germany, then crushed, milled, conditioned at 350 to 400 degrees Celsius and finely ground.
fields.precautions: EFSA could not conclude on target-animal safety of the assessed natrolite-phonolite feed preparation in 2023. Risks associated with possible nanoparticles could not be assessed for animals, consumers or users; handling also raised sensitisation concerns. These findings concern the specified feed material and do not establish a typical direct human-food use.

fields.overview: Perlite is a naturally occurring aluminosilicate volcanic-glass material. The reviewed feed preparation does not establish a typical direct use in human food.

Safety conclusions for the animals applied to particular tested or extrapolated categories, with no conclusion for the remaining categories. It should not be treated as a plant wax or as a description of every synthetic cetyl-palmitate preparation.

fields.overview: Lanolin is the waxy material recovered from sheep wool. It contains a complex mixture of long-chain esters, together with smaller amounts of related alcohols, acids and hydrocarbons. Its protective role on wool and its wax-like consistency distinguish it from a simple triglyceride oil. FDA lists lanolin as a plasticising material in chewing-gum base. That specified gum-base use is a different technological role from the historical glazing classification.
fields.origin: Animal-derived material recovered from sheep wool during wool washing and separation, then refined. It is a complex wool-wax preparation rather than a single purified molecule.
fields.dietary_restrictions: Lanolin is an animal-derived wool wax and is not vegan. The reviewed identity source does not establish vegetarian suitability or halal and kosher certification of a food-use preparation.
fields.uses: Used as a plasticising or softening material in chewing-gum base under 21 CFR 172.615.
